notes.claim: To expand a bracket, the factor outside is multiplied by each term inside, not just the first.
Expanding a bracket gives a second way of writing the same expression, so the value does not change.
The resistance formula R = R₀(1 + αΔT) has a bracket that can be expanded in the same way.
With a current I through resistors in series, the voltage V = IR₁ + IR₂ + IR₃ = I(R₁ + R₂ + R₃), the same expansion with a letter outside.
A minus in front of a bracket must be multiplied into both terms, so x − (a − b) is x − a + b, and a number check shows the slip.

sources.title: Solve equations with brackets - KS3 Maths - BBC Bitesize
sources.quote: Expanding brackets does not change the value of an expression . It is two ways of writing the same expression.

sources.quote: As can be seen -5 is not equal to 3 so the formula is incorrect. The error was that the negative sign must be multiplied into both terms in the bracket leaving x-(a-b) = x-a+b.
